items.note: AEA RCT registration only (AEARCTR-0014305, no paper yet): engineering-student venture teams randomized to training on using generative AI for early-stage idea development versus traditional creativity training; primary outcomes include external judges' grades of problem relevance and value proposition (innovation); randomization appears to be at team level (at least 130 teams per search notes), and results may not exist yet.

Natural experiment with difference-in-differences on 1.5 million Change.org petitions around the launch of an in-platform write-with-AI tool; AI access increased petition homogeneity but did not improve outcomes; abstract from the arXiv version (2511.13949), same study as the Nature Human Behaviour article; tool use is not assigned to people.

Controlled experiment with 123 product innovators in three conditions (no AI, moderate AI assistance, high AI assistance) on product idea generation, scoring number, originality, and feasibility of ideas; inverted-U pattern with moderate assistance best; assignment method not stated in the abstract.

Quasi-experiment with 97 third-graders in China, classes randomly assigned to a generative-AI chatbot (n = 48) or a search engine (n = 49) during science inquiry learning; chatbot group scored higher on problem quality and problem-posing ability; randomization is by intact class (likely two classes), and whether problem posing counts as a creativity outcome needs a check at full text.

Preregistered online experiment (N = 554) and museum naturalistic experiment (N = 36,198) giving real-time AI originality feedback from trained scoring models on human ideas and sketches; feedback raised originality; next stage should check whether the feedback models count as generative AI (they evaluate rather than generate) and how conditions were assigned.

HCI system paper (Creo, multi-stage sketch-to-image generation) with a comparative user study against a one-shot text-to-image baseline; embedding analysis shows Creo outputs are less homogeneous; abstract gives no N (search notes say 15 participants, within-subjects counterbalanced), so it likely falls below the 50-person threshold.

Online experiment (n = 102) comparing idea generation with AI support versus working alone, scored on Torrance dimensions (fluency, elaboration, flexibility, originality); AI support raised fluency, elaboration, and flexibility but lowered originality; ECIS 2024 proceedings, abstract from the AIS eLibrary page; assignment not stated.

Engineering (N = 99) and psychology (N = 212) students wrote an initial engineering-design solution, evaluated pre-generated GPT-3.5 ideas, and revised; originality and effectiveness of solutions were rated; the only AI contrast appears to be within-person before versus after AI exposure with fixed order (no no-AI comparison group in the abstract), so it may fail eligibility at full text; total N is 311.

Within-subject experiment with 40 university students solving a design problem with and without ChatGPT-4o; consensus assessment found AI slightly raised originality and usefulness of design sketches; below the 50-person threshold; condition order randomization not stated.

Two studies of children telling stories with a social robot driven by an LLM fine-tuned for creative versus non-creative behavior (Wizard-of-Oz study N = 38, autonomous study N = 103); children's fluency, flexibility, and elaboration were higher with the creative autonomous robot; the contrast is one AI configuration versus another, with no no-AI arm.
